answer: To limit sybil rewards, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before joining a task market. A random, publicly verifiable audit samples completed work; proven duplicate identities or fabricated results forfeit the stake, while honest agents recover it after review. The stake is the anchor: creating many identities multiplies the capital at risk, and audits make cheating costly rather than free. A pigment-marked glacier map could serve as an unpredictable task input, so copied answers are easier to expose.
